data.why: The dashboard loads panel/data/stress.csv by default (already shipped in the repo) and accepts CSV uploads via its FileInput widget; the other two test fixtures (CO2.csv, crying.csv) are real example datasets the project's own test suite uses, suitable for exercising the upload path with different column counts and variable names.

goals: Load a CSV of model inputs and one output variable and see the default sensitivity-analysis dashboard populate
Identify which input variables matter most by reading the sensitivity indices table and choosing inputs for decomposition
Run simulation decomposition on the top-explaining inputs and read off the auto-selected scenarios reaching ~80% explained variance
Compare the output distribution as a stacked histogram versus a boxplot, color-coded by scenario
Recolor individual states with the color pickers to make a published-quality figure
Export the computed sensitivity indices, scenario table, and state table as a CSV for reporting
Generate a synthetic sample (second app, /sampling) to explore Monte Carlo / quasi-Monte Carlo sampling designs before running a simulation

review.summary: The tree follows SimDec's stated pipeline (sensitivity indices, then scenarios, then colour-coded chart, then export) plus the sampling app, at a sensible depth, and the screens I opened mostly show what the nodes say. It needs small fixes before filing: add the interpretation step and the sampling tasks for distributions and export, correct three code-checkable claims (the 4-input cap, the Docs panel, the export blocks), and replace the download citations that show no download.
